page.title: Dolphin Watching & Snorkeling Combo in Marbella: Best of Both

data.meta_description: Book a dolphin watching snorkeling combo in Marbella. Spot wild dolphins off Puerto Banús, then snorkel in hidden coves. From €749 for 2h. Reserve now.
data.summary: A dolphin watching snorkeling combo in Marbella combines the thrill of spotting wild dolphins in the Mediterranean with a refreshing snorkel in secluded coves. Departing from Puerto Banús, this half-day experience suits families and small groups, with prices starting at €749 for two hours.

Snorkeling stops at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés
Up to 11 passengers on selected boats

faq.q: How long does the dolphin watching snorkeling combo last?
faq.a: Most combo trips run 3–4 hours, but you can tailor the duration. Our Tier A boats, the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39, are available from €749 for 2 hours up to €2,299 for 8 hours. For a relaxed pace with both dolphin spotting and snorkeling, we recommend 4 hours.

faq.q: Which boats are available for the combo?
faq.a: You can choose from our Tier A boats: the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 passengers) or the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 passengers). Both depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. For larger groups, ask about our bigger yachts via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What is included in the price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). The snorkeling gear (masks, fins, snorkels) is provided free of charge on combo trips.

We can't guarantee sightings, as dolphins are wild animals, but the waters off Marbella are home to several pods. Sightings are most common in the morning, and our skippers know the best spots. On days when dolphins are elusive, you'll still enjoy the coastal views and snorkeling.

faq.q: Do we need to be experienced snorkelers?
faq.a: No, the combo is suitable for beginners. The skipper will anchor in calm, shallow coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where you can snorkel at your own pace. Life jackets and buoyancy aids are available. Children aged 5+ are welcome with adult supervision.

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the sea breeze. You might want a waterproof camera to capture the dolphins. We provide all drinks and snacks, so no need to bring your own. Remember to wear non-slip shoes on the boat.

You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before departure. If the weather is poor and the skipper decides it's unsafe to sail, we'll offer a full refund or reschedule. No-shows are non-refundable.

data.body_html:
Combine two of Marbella's best sea experiences in one unforgettable trip: a dolphin watching snorkeling combo. Departing from Puerto Banús, you'll cruise the Mediterranean in search of wild dolphins, then drop anchor in a secluded cove for a snorkeling session. With prices starting at €749 for 2 hours, this combo is a smart way to see more of the coast without breaking the bank.

Why Choose a Combo Trip?

Separate dolphin tours and snorkeling trips can eat up your holiday time. A combo packs both into a single outing, maximising your time on the water. You'll spend the first part of the trip scanning the horizon for dolphins, then switch to snorkeling when the skipper finds a calm spot. It's perfect for families, couples, and small groups who want variety.

What to Expect on the Water

Your skipper will head west from Puerto Banús towards the waters off Cabopino or Estepona, where dolphins are frequently spotted. The boat slows down as dolphins approach, giving you time to watch them play in the bow wave. After about an hour of dolphin watching, the skipper steers to a sheltered cove like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for snorkeling. The clear, calm waters here are ideal for beginners and children.

Our Boats for the Combo

We offer two Tier A boats for this experience, both departing from Puerto Banús:

What's Included

  • Licensed skipper and fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Snorkeling equipment (masks, fins, snorkels)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

Best Time for Dolphin Sightings

Dolphins are year-round residents in the Alboran Sea, but sightings are most reliable from May to October. Morning departures tend to have calmer seas and more active dolphins. The sea temperature in summer averages 22–26°C, making snorkeling comfortable. Even if dolphins are shy, the coastal scenery of the Golden Mile and the Sierra Blanca mountains makes the trip worthwhile.

How to Book

Booking is simple. Visit our boat rental Marbella page to see all available options, or head to the [hub](/) for a full overview. For the dolphin watching snorkeling combo, select the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 and choose your duration. You can also message us on WhatsApp for custom requests or to add extras like a jet ski.
